A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same complete 22-page paper, including Appendices A–K. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish identical substantive content; only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its link differ.

before.justification: v3 reports original XLM-R ABX measurements, linguistic probing, cross-lingual transfer evaluations, and checkpoint/source-selection analyses in Sections 4–5 and the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Table 1, the discrimination plots, and the appendix analyses.

M1.justification: The language and meaning discrimination procedures, embedding extraction, cosine-distance scoring, and Algorithms 1–3 are identical.

E1.justification: Both retain the same WMT24++ ABX coverage and UD/PUD, WikiAnn, and XNLI evaluations, with identical language/task membership in Appendix C.

E2.justification: The retrieval comparison in Section 4.1, final-checkpoint comparator in Appendix H, and random-source selection baseline in Appendix K are unchanged.

E3.justification: The checkpoint and layer settings, approximately 100,000 triplets per condition, probing splits, early stopping, metrics, and testing procedures are identical.

E4.justification: Both contain the same validation controls, triplet-sampling robustness check, LD–MD relationship analyses, and ABX-guided checkpoint/source-selection studies.

E5.justification: Both report six seeded probing runs, five random ABX subsamples, and identical uncertainty and significance reporting, including the Wilcoxon test in Appendix H and confidence intervals in Figure 11.

E6.justification: Table 1, all plotted results, and numerical findings in the appendices match. For example, Appendix H retains the checkpoint-selection improvement in 29 of 36 languages and mean improvement of 0.034 ± 0.048.

T1.justification: The triplet definitions, ABX scoring equations, tie handling, and regression formulation are identical. No theoretical argument or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain identical claims about training-free ABX evaluation, form/meaning dynamics, and relationships with downstream performance.

C2.justification: Interpretations and limitations are identical, including the partial form–meaning trade-off, weak connection to NLI performance, single-encoder scope, and distinction between discrimination and representational separation.

D1.justification: The model/checkpoint descriptions, sampling and scoring pseudocode, experimental details, and reported resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the bibliography contain the same cited works and positioning relative to probing, multilingual alignment, and earlier ABX research.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v3, dated 22 Sep 2025, to v4, dated 19 Nov 2025, with its self-link updated accordingly. Paper wording, authorship, and section structure are unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures, tables, algorithms, captions, and placement are identical. Rendered pages match throughout, apart from the version/date stamp text on page 1.

improvement.justification: The substantive text, empirical evidence, mathematical content, explanations, and visual presentation are identical, including Appendices A–K. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and self-link does not meaningfully alter the paper's overall quality.
